name: BA Geography
title: BA Geography
intro: The BA Geography roadmap: admission, physical and human geography, GIS skills, fieldwork and career routes.

phases.title: Class 11–12: subjects that help
phases.summary: Any stream is accepted; Geography, Economics, Environmental Studies and basic Maths give the easiest start.
points: BA Geography admits students from Arts, Commerce and Science in most universities, with a minimum Class 12 percentage fixed by the college.
Subjects that help in school: Geography, Economics, Environmental Studies and basic Maths.
Build reading, writing and discussion habits; humanities degrees reward them from the first semester.
Check whether your target university asks for a specific subject combination in CUET-UG.
facts: Geography, Economics, Environmental Studies and basic Maths

phases.title: Entrance and admission cycle
phases.summary: Central universities use CUET-UG; state universities and colleges use merit or their own tests.
points: Register for CUET-UG in the NTA window and choose the domain subjects asked by your target universities.
Apply to the university counselling or admission portal and rank colleges and course combinations.
State and private universities publish merit lists or run entrance tests and interviews.
Follow seat-allotment rounds and confirm admission with documents and fees by the deadline.

phases.title: Year 1: foundation papers
phases.summary: Core introductory papers plus ability-enhancement courses.
points: Core papers: Physical Geography, Human Geography, Cartography and Maps, and Environmental Studies.
You also take language, environmental studies and skill-based courses under NEP.
Learn how to write academic assignments, cite sources and present.
Join the department society and start reading beyond the syllabus.

phases.title: Year 2–3: depth and specialisation
phases.summary: Advanced papers, electives and a dissertation or project.
points: Year 2 core: Geography of India, Climatology, Population and Settlement Geography, and Statistical Methods.
Year 3 core and electives: Remote Sensing and GIS, Regional Planning, Disaster Management, and Fieldwork-based projects.
Under NEP, a fourth Honours year with research is available in many universities.
You complete internships and projects, and write a dissertation where required.

phases.title: Skills and internships
phases.summary: Build practical skills that employers and masters’ programmes value.
points: Learn: GIS and remote sensing software (QGIS, ArcGIS), map making, field survey methods, basic statistics and report writing.
Do internships with NGOs, research centres, media houses, museums, think tanks or companies relevant to your field.
Take online courses on SWAYAM, NPTEL or Coursera to add certificates.
Prepare a portfolio of writing, projects and research notes.

phases.title: After the degree
phases.summary: Choose a master’s, a professional course, a government exam or a job.
points: Further study: MA/MSc Geography, MSc GIS and Remote Sensing, urban and regional planning, environmental studies or disaster management.
Exams: CUET-PG, UGC NET, UPSC (Geography optional) and state PSCs.
Teaching and research: MA, UGC NET/JRF and PhD.
Government and civil services exams are open to graduates from any discipline.
facts: CUET-PG, UGC NET, UPSC (Geography optional) and state PSCs
